As an engineer my must-have feature is screen sharing with collaborative annotation... it was the epitome of bloat. It takes a screenshot of the presenter's desktop and starts a whiteboard session, taking ~30 seconds to enable, and the screen can't be interacted with until annotation stops.
Remember that Microsoft has had a UC/chat app forever. Teams in comparison to Skype for Business is an improvement.
Everything in Teams ranges from "utter crap" to "half assed effort but mostly still just crap". It's the most "me-too" app I've ever had the displeasure of being forced to use.
When I end a meeting, Teams helpfully shows a window that states something like "meetings is just one of the many things we do!" to which I want to reply, "maybe you shouldn't do more".
Their products targeted to other programmers seem nicer to work with, e.g. VS Code, C#, SQL Server. The products aimed at 'knowledge workers', like Teams and SharePoint, are garbage.

Absolutely incredibly garbage, how do they have the audacity to ship something so bad? I experienced a situation where everyone could see and hear only about half of the other meeting participants, but not the same set for everyone.
It certainly doesn't help that it's an Electron app and a fat one at that.
An old employer of mine used Teams and my biggest problem was just sending messages to other people. If you go back and edit styled text it removes the style and you have to work to get it back.
Teams is horribly unintuitive to use. The UI is much worse than Slack. Took me long to realise I was looking at the chat window and to follow along the threads.
I had to rename files with a # in the filename since that character is forbidden in filenames uploaded into Teams. Also you can't attach a .json file... though renaming it to .json.txt works.

The most frustrating and immediate drawback is the low information density. I can still see only about 20% of the information in a chat that I can with Slack. Also the automatic conversion of things like ;) to animated emoji... please give me an option to turn this off.
For extra fun, block access to the telemetry endpoint and watch Teams' memory footprint bloat to crazy levels as the data accumulates and re-attempts the sending.

I collect my complaints in a confluence page: You can't link to conversations. The UI between a Teams channel and a chat with multiple people is not consistent - direct chats don't support threading or  code blocks. Notifications in channels are easy to miss.

Search is abysmal. When clicking a result, you jump to the message but it is devoid of context. We routinely have issues with images not displaying and messages going completely missing in 1:1 chats even after restarting the client.
MS have not implemented muting as a feature. You can't unsubscribe yourself from admin channels. Unavoidable alerts that any idiot on any channel can annoy people with.

My main beefs with Teams are: Performance - it's just far too damn slow to switch views. Awkward to switch back to a channel while on a call. Connectivity issues force restarts occasionally, which takes too long.
One thing I do like: switching from Slack to Teams resulted in much higher signal-to-noise ratio - way less distracting guff being posted than on Slack.
I prefer Teams to Slack. I like the built-in screen sharing and that you can share a window rather than a screen. The voice/video Teams meetings are pretty handy for remote standups.

My team hated Teams, I tolerated it. Until one day I'd just had enough of the UX - the biggest issue was the threading; it truly beggars belief. We ended up using multi-user IM messages instead of channels.
So glad Microsoft installed teams on our server with an update even though we never asked for it.
